facts.text: Mountain Village began as a seasonal Yup'ik fish camp, grew into a trading and mission hub in the early 1900s, and opened its post office in 1923.
Mountain Village experiences a continental climate with temperatures swinging from -44°F in winter to 80°F in summer, and 44 inches of snow each year.
Permafrost patches across Mountain Village create elevated plateaus on abandoned floodplains, limiting vegetation to low shrubs, grasses, and mosses adapted to wet soils.
The 4.3‑square‑mile community sits at the base of 500‑foot Azachorok Mountain and lies within the Yukon Delta National Wildlife Refuge, preserving Yup'ik traditions.
Mountain Village faces flooding, erosion, wildfires, earthquakes, severe weather, and distant volcanic activity from Ingakslugwat Hills 50 miles south.
High wind speeds support a test wind turbine operated by the Alaska Village Electric Cooperative, supplementing diesel power in Mountain Village.
